title: autotune: cost-optimization defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Riya Patel
description: Context: We have a growing set of customer workloads where suboptimal batching/caching defaults and lack of first-class quantization presets are driving unnecessary GPU spend. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) sensible runtime defaults and an autotune pass for batching and KV-prefix caching, 2) a set of validated quantization profiles (fp16/4bit/4bit-compat) with automatic compatibility checks, and 3) a lightweight unit-economics (UEcon) tooling surface (CLI + internal dashboard hooks) to estimate per-token cost impact of settings. Motivation: reduce out-of-the-box cost for common request distributions and empower customers/operators to understand trade-offs without deep inference expertise. What I changed: - runtime/autotune: add a two-phase autotune that samples live traffic (or synthetic traces) and recommends batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, and prefix_cache_ttl defaults; fallback to conservative values when variance is high. - runtime/batching: introduce per-model policy templates (low-latency, balanced, cost-optimized) and a simple scoring function for selection. - runtime/cache: enable prefix-KV default caching with LRU + size-based eviction and TTL heuristics tuned per model family. - models/quant-profiles: add curated quant profiles for gpt-like and llama-like families, compatibility matrix, and safety checks that block unsafe profiles for eval/production. - tooling/uecon: CLI command `redwood uecon analyze` to run offline estimates and a telemetry hook to surface predicted vs observed cost in internal dashboard. - docs/ and examples/: add quickstart guide and migration notes for Dedicated/Private. Testing and validation: unit + integration tests for autotune logic, end-to-end perf regressions measured against perf-canary benchmarks (20% median cost reduction in cost-optimized template on conversational microbenchmarks), and canary rollout across 5% of traffic for two weeks. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-3421) - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks + canary - [x] docs & migration notes - [x] security review (no secrets or new surface exposed) Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if 5% uplift in median latency or 10% regression in quality evals. Related: ENG-3421, ENG-3510, PM-129. Notes: this PR touches runtime decision logic; the defaults are conservative and can be overridden by per-customer policies. All changes are backwards compatible; no API break.
